requirement: `run_named_query` MUST accept a declared `requirement/query` name and return the matching source node IDs and their data. Agents read the relevant nodes with `read_node`.
rationale:
The requirement has two testable obligations. `run_named_query` must accept a declared `<requirement>/<query>` name and return the matching source node IDs with their data. The returned nodes must also be readable with `read_node`.

**Accepting a declared query and returning matches.** `src/authoring/domain_tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[domain_discovery_returns_readable_nodes_without_recording_their_contents]` calls `RunNamedQuery` with `requirements.rule/checkers`. It asserts three sites. Each entry has exactly two keys, `node` (a u64) and `data` (an object). Each node's cached data equals the returned `data`. Each node's source selector contains `fn[check_`, so the query returns the expected sites.

**Reading the nodes.** The same test calls `cx.read(&node)` on every returned node and asserts three dependencies afterwards. Before those reads it asserts `cx.dependencies().is_empty()`, so running the query itself reads nothing. It also reads a looked-up example node with `read_snapshot` and checks its content.

**Invalid names.** The same test checks that `malformed` returns the error "expected <requirement>/<query>" and that `absent/query` returns "unknown requirement". The requirement text does not name these cases, so they are extra coverage.

**Other tests.** `src/authoring/domain_tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[named_query_errors_identify_the_source_without_exposing_a_line_number]` covers a malformed declared query, which the text does not name. The tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/structural.rs` check the structural rule engine and innermost-node ownership. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[explicit_ignored_reads_return_an_error_and_the_assessment_continues]` checks the `run_named_query` tool description and the structural search tool through the CLI. They support the feature but are not needed to establish adequacy.

I found no obligation without a test, and no assertion that would pass behavior violating the text.
